name: Skoffin
body:
SKOFFÍN
CR 4

This mangy beast, resembling a feral, ashen-furred cat with a bushy fox-like tail and glowing eyes, seems barely to be clinging to life with its hair falling out in clumps and its flesh rotting and sloughing off to show exposed bone.

XP 1,200
NE Tiny magical beast
Init +8; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, tremorsense 10 ft.; Perception +10

DEFENSE

AC 18, touch 17, flat-footed 13 (+4 Dex, +1 dodge, +1 natural, +2 size)
hp 27 (5d10)
Fort +4, Ref +8, Will +4
DR 5/silver

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft., burrow 20 ft., climb 30 ft.; earth glide
Melee 2 claws +11 (1d3-1 plus 1d6 bleed), bite +11 (1d4-1 plus attach)
Space 2-1/2 ft.; Reach 0 ft.
Special Attacks attach (bite), lethal glare, smother, strangle

STATISTICS

Str 8, Dex 18, Con 10, Int 10, Wis 16, Cha 14
Base Atk +5; CMB +2; CMD 17 (21 vs. trip)
Feats Dodge, Improved Initiative, Mobility, Weapon Finesse B
Skills Perception +10, Stealth +19
Languages Common, Undercommon
SQ deep breath, earth glide, evasion

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Deep Breath (Ex)

The skoffín can hold its breath for about 1 hour.

Lethal Glare (Ex)

As a bonus action the skoffín glares in a 30-foot cone. Each creature it can see in the area must succeed at a DC 14 Fortitude save or gain 1 temporary negative level. If the skoffín sees its own reflection or the reflection of any other creature in the area and the reflected creature is within 30 feet of the skoffín and in bright light, the reflected creature is also affected. This is a death effect. The save DC is Charisma-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment cold coastlines or plains
Organization solitary, pair, or clowder (3–5)
Treasure none

These little beasts are insidious killers resembling a cross between a housecat and a fox. Their gaze can kill even if they are unseen, and they often make a game of killing as many larger creatures as they can without being spotted.

Skoffíns dig burrows like foxes to breed in, and they are quick diggers within minutes of birth. They give birth to small litters of live pups distinguishable from other small mammalian predators by their open eyes. Luckily, the pups do not develop the killing gaze until they mature.
